title: Madhuri Dixit Hides a Dead Body in a Netflix Dark Comedy. Maa Behen Drops Wednesday.
excerpt: Suresh Triveni's crime-comedy pairs Madhuri with Triptii Dimri and newcomer Dharna Durga as a dysfunctional mother-daughter trio spiralling through a cover-up. It streams globally on June 4.
body:
A dead man lies in the kitchen. The three women standing over him have not called the police. They have not called an ambulance. They have, instead, started arguing about whose fault this is.

That is the premise of *Maa Behen*, the new Hindi-language dark comedy thriller arriving on Netflix on June 4. Directed by Suresh Triveni — who last helmed the Anil Kapoor-starrer *Subedaar* — the film stars Madhuri Dixit as Rekha, a single mother whose already-fractured household takes a sharp turn toward the criminal when a body shows up where the groceries should be.

## The Cast Makes This Worth Watching

Triptii Dimri plays Jaya, the older daughter who has inherited her mother's sharp tongue but not her patience. Dharna Durga, a relative newcomer who has been generating quiet buzz in promotional interviews, plays Sushma, the younger sister. The trailer shows all three women oscillating between panic, blame, and surprisingly practical disposal logistics.

Ravi Kishan plays Gupta Ji, a nosy neighbour whose conservative instincts and proximity to the crime scene make him the trio's biggest threat. The supporting cast includes Geetanjali Kulkarni, Arunoday Singh, Shardul Bhardwaj, and Jatin Sarna as Rekha's husband — whose role appears to be mostly in flashback.

## Suresh Triveni's Signature Territory

Triveni has built a reputation for films about women navigating impossible situations with dark wit. *Tumhari Sulu* explored a housewife who becomes a late-night radio host; *Jalsa* put Vidya Balan and Shefali Shah on opposite sides of a hit-and-run. *Maa Behen* fits the pattern — women with contradictions, forced into choices that reveal who they actually are. The screenplay is by Pooja Tolani, and the production comes from Vikram Malhotra's Abundantia Entertainment and Triveni's own Opening Image Films.

## Why This Matters for the Diaspora

For NRIs, this is the kind of Indian-language film that would never have reached US or UK screens a decade ago. Netflix's global day-and-date release means audiences in New York, London, Toronto, and Sydney will watch it at the same time as viewers in Mumbai. No theatrical delay, no waiting for an OTT window. That shift has made Hindi cinema's mid-budget, performance-driven films — the ones that don't need ₹500-crore spectacle budgets — suddenly accessible to the very audience that grew up on Madhuri Dixit's filmography.

Madhuri herself addressed the film's tone in a recent interview. When asked whether she would commit the same cover-up as Rekha, she paused and said she would probably do fewer "kaands" than her on-screen daughters — but did not rule it out entirely.

## The Promotional Controversy

A minor dust-up preceded the release. Social media users accused Madhuri and Triptii of sidelining Dharna Durga during promotional events. Both actresses responded, calling the speculation unfounded and pointing out that promotional seating and interview formats are controlled by production teams, not co-stars. The controversy is the kind of social-media cycle that typically dies within 48 hours — but it has, inadvertently, raised Dharna Durga's profile considerably.

## The Bottom Line

*Maa Behen* streams globally on Netflix starting June 4. If you have ever watched your mother and sister argue over something trivial and thought, "Imagine if the stakes were actually life and death," this film has anticipated your thought experiment and filmed it.

**Sources:** Netflix India, Bollywood Hungama, Filmfare, Zoom TV Entertainment
